name: Do Kwon
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Terraform Labs in January 2018 with Daniel Shin, launching the Terra blockchain and later the Luna/UST ecosystem that reached multi-billion market cap before collapsing in 2022.
early_history_summary: Born in Seoul on 6 September 1991, Kwon attended Daewon Foreign Language High School and earned a BS in computer science from Stanford in 2015. He briefly worked as a software engineer at Microsoft and Apple, then returned to South Korea in 2016 to found Anyfi before co-founding Terraform Labs in early 2018 at age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Seoul, South Korea; family financial and professional background not documented in reviewed sources beyond later reports that Anyfi funding involved an incubator linked to a co-founder's parents.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford CS, crypto structural wave, co-founder Shin, Asia crypto markets
evidence_summary: Kwon's Stanford CS degree and brief Big Tech engineering roles provided technical credibility before he founded Anyfi and then Terraform Labs at 26. The 2018 crypto boom was a strong structural wave; co-founder Daniel Shin added complementary domain and network. Family background is sparsely documented. Later Forbes 30 Under 30 recognition (2019) and the Terra ecosystem's growth (then catastrophic collapse and fraud conviction) define his trajectory more than early-family advantages.
starting_point: Born in Seoul, South Korea, 6 September 1991; attended elite Daewon Foreign Language High School; family socioeconomic detail not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Convicted of fraud related to Terraform Labs; sentenced in December 2025 to 15 years in U.S. federal prison after extradition from Montenegro.

trajectory.event: Graduated Stanford with a BS in computer science; brief software engineering roles at Microsoft and Apple.
Returned to South Korea and founded Anyfi, a mesh networking startup.
Co-founded Terraform Labs with Daniel Shin and launched the Terra blockchain/Luna ecosystem.
Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia (Finance & Venture Capital).
TerraUSD and Luna collapsed, wiping out roughly $45B in market value within a week.
Arrested in Montenegro while traveling on forged documents; later charged with multiple U.S. fraud counts.
Pleaded guilty to fraud charges and was sentenced to 15 years in U.S. federal prison.

name: Feross Aboukhadijeh
milestone_by_age_26: Built and launched YouTube Instant in September 2010 at age 19 while a Stanford student and Facebook intern; the site went viral (hundreds of thousands to 1M+ visitors) and drew a public job offer from YouTube CEO Chad Hurley.
early_history_summary: Grew up in the Sacramento area and began building websites around age 13–14 (FreeTheFlash drew hundreds of thousands of visitors in 2006). As a high schooler he founded Study Notes (AP study tools) and interned at Intel. At Stanford he interned at Facebook (Groups) and Quora, then launched YouTube Instant in 2010 and later PeerCDN (acquired by Yahoo in 2013).
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Sacramento-area high school (Oak Ridge HS) and early self-taught web building.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford, Facebook internship, early web viral products, open-source community, Silicon Valley
evidence_summary: Feross shipped widely used web projects from high school onward (FreeTheFlash, Study Notes) and at 19 built YouTube Instant, which attracted major press and a CEO job offer. Stanford CS plus Facebook/Quora internships embedded him in elite tech networks. Later PeerCDN (Yahoo acquisition), WebTorrent, Standard JS, and Socket (raised tens of millions; ~$1B valuation reported with Series C) show continued open-source and founder leverage. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Grew up in the Sacramento, California area; began self-taught web development in early teens; family class/occupation detail not documented.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Socket (developer supply-chain security); company has raised large venture rounds (including reported Series C around a $1B valuation); formerly Stanford web-security lecturer.

trajectory.event: FreeTheFlash entertainment site reached hundreds of thousands of unique visitors while he was in high school.
Founded Study Notes, AP/college-prep study tools later used by hundreds of thousands of students monthly.
Launched YouTube Instant; went viral and received a public job offer from YouTube CEO Chad Hurley.
PeerCDN acquired by Yahoo; he joined Yahoo engineering.
Created WebTorrent, a BitTorrent client for the browser that became a major open-source project.
Founded Socket, a developer-first software supply-chain security company.
Continued as Socket CEO after multi-stage venture funding and large enterprise adoption.

name: Lenore Blum
milestone_by_age_26: Received a Ph.D. in mathematics from MIT in 1968 at age 25 for a dissertation connecting model theory and differential algebra (Generalized Algebraic Theories: A Model Theoretic Approach), supervised by Gerald Sacks.
early_history_summary: Born Lenore Carol Epstein in New York City on 18 December 1942 to a Jewish family; mother was a science teacher. The family moved to Caracas, Venezuela when she was nine. She finished high school at 16, began architecture at Carnegie Tech, switched to mathematics with Alan Perlis's help, transferred to Simmons College, cross-registered at MIT, and completed her MIT PhD in 1968 at 25.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family in New York City; mother was a science teacher. Family moved to Caracas when she was nine for her father's business with a relative.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a science teacher, providing some STEM-oriented household context; father's business details beyond Venezuela relocation are limited.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT PhD, early specialization, science-teacher mother, gender barrier friction, marriage to Manuel Blum
evidence_summary: Blum finished high school early, entered college at 16, and earned an MIT PhD at 25 despite institutional barriers (Princeton would not admit women graduate students when her first advisor moved). Mentorship (Alan Perlis, Gerald Sacks) and elite MIT training were catalytic. Later work (Blum-Blum-Shub generator, Blum–Shub–Smale machine, AWM leadership, CMU Women@SCS) made her a major figure in theoretical CS and women-in-STEM advocacy. Married to Turing Award winner Manuel Blum; son Avrim Blum is also a noted CS researcher.
starting_point: Born 18 December 1942 in New York City to a Jewish family; mother a science teacher; relocated to Caracas, Venezuela at age 9.
current_position: Professor-in-residence (EECS) at UC Berkeley; emeritus Distinguished Career Professor of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon; president of the Association for Mathematical Consciousness Science; elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2024.

trajectory.event: Finished Venezuelan high school and enrolled at Carnegie Institute of Technology (later switched to mathematics).
Earned BS in mathematics from Simmons College while taking MIT courses.
Received PhD in mathematics from MIT for model-theoretic work on algebraic theories.
Co-founded the Association for Women in Mathematics.
Founded the mathematics and computer science department at Mills College.
Co-authored the Blum–Blum–Shub cryptographically secure pseudorandom generator paper.
Became Distinguished Career Professor of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University.
Elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

name: Michael Glukhovsky
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded RethinkDB (YC Summer 2009) and later worked in developer products at Stripe, but no reliable public birth year was found, so age ≤26 at the founding milestone could not be independently verified.
early_history_summary: Attended Stony Brook University (about 2006–2010), specializing in human-computer interaction; co-founded RethinkDB with Slava Akhmechet and participated in Y Combinator Summer 2009. After RethinkDB shut down, he moved to Stripe developer products.
evidence_summary: RethinkDB founding and YC S09 are documented, and college timing suggests he was likely young, but without a sourced birth year the age-26 eligibility criterion cannot be confirmed under the rubric.

name: Lucas Beyer
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Diplom studies at RWTH Aachen ran roughly 2006–2012 and PhD in computer vision 2013–2018; defining work (Google Brain/DeepMind staff scientist from 2018, Vision Transformer co-authorship 2020) occurred after typical age-26 window.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Belgium wanting to make video games; studied mechanical/computational engineering at RWTH Aachen, completed a computer-vision PhD there in 2018, then joined Google Brain/DeepMind as a staff research scientist and later moved among Meta, OpenAI, and related labs.
evidence_summary: Career-defining AI research roles and papers arrived after PhD completion in 2018. Birth year not public, but education timeline places major milestones after age 26. Marked ineligible.

name: David Oppenheimer
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Received a PhD from UC Berkeley in 2005 and joined Google thereafter, working on Borg/Omega and later Kubernetes scheduling; defining infrastructure contributions came after graduate training.
early_history_summary: PhD from UC Berkeley (2005); long Google career including Borg whitepaper co-authorship and Kubernetes SIG Scheduling / multi-tenancy leadership.
evidence_summary: Documented impact is on Borg/Kubernetes after a 2005 PhD. Without birth year and with a postdoc/industry path typical of age late-20s+, no ≤26 material milestone is established.

name: Robert Tappan Morris
milestone_by_age_26: Released the Morris worm on 2 November 1988 at age 22 while a Cornell graduate student—the first widely propagating Internet worm—leading to the first conviction under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.
early_history_summary: Born 8 November 1965 to Bell Labs cryptographer/computer scientist Robert Morris and Anne Farlow Morris. Grew up in Millington, New Jersey, attended Peck School and Delbarton School, then Harvard College. Entered Cornell's CS PhD program and released the Morris worm in 1988 from MIT machines to obscure its origin.
family_context_summary: Father Robert Morris was a pioneering Unix/Multics cryptographer at Bell Labs and later chief scientist of the NSA National Computer Security Center; mother Anne Farlow Morris. Household immersed in advanced computing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a leading computer security and Unix figure at Bell Labs/NSA, giving direct domain exposure, tools culture, and technical fluency from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bell Labs father, Harvard, early Unix/security exposure, rare home computing environment
evidence_summary: Morris's father was a foundational Unix/security researcher, creating an unusually strong family-domain and tools advantage. Harvard and Cornell provided elite training; high-school password-cracking anecdotes and the 1988 worm show deep early systems skill. Later he co-founded Viaweb (sold to Yahoo), co-founded Y Combinator, and became a tenured MIT professor and National Academy of Engineering member.
starting_point: Born 8 November 1965 in the United States to Bell Labs computer scientist Robert Morris and Anne Farlow Morris; raised in Millington, New Jersey.
current_position: Professor of Computer Science and Engineering at MIT EECS/CSAIL; longtime Y Combinator partner; National Academy of Engineering member (2019).

trajectory.event: Graduated from Delbarton School; later attended Harvard College.
Released the Morris worm, the first widely propagating Internet worm.
Convicted under the CFAA; sentenced to probation, community service, and a fine.
Co-founded Viaweb with Paul Graham (sold to Yahoo in 1998 for ~$49M).
Received Harvard PhD and joined MIT as assistant professor.
Co-founded Y Combinator with Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, and Trevor Blackwell.
Awarded tenure at MIT.
Elected to the National Academy of Engineering.

name: Jeff Bonwick
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Joined Sun Microsystems around 1991 after a Berkeley EE degree; invented/led ZFS development in the early 2000s (prototype ~2001, announcement ~2004), well after age 26 for a typical early-1990s college graduate.
early_history_summary: Electrical engineering degree from UC Berkeley; long Sun Microsystems career as engineer, Sun Fellow, and storage CTO; invented and led ZFS; later co-founded DSSD.
evidence_summary: ZFS and later DSSD define his reputation but occurred mid-career at Sun. Birth year not found; education/career timeline places signature work after age 26.

name: Mihai Alisie
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Bitcoin Magazine with Vitalik Buterin in 2011 and was an Ethereum co-founder (late 2013), but no reliable public birth year was found, so age ≤26 at those milestones could not be verified.
early_history_summary: Romanian entrepreneur who contacted Vitalik Buterin in 2011 to start Bitcoin Magazine, later joined Ethereum's founding team, helped set up Swiss/Crypto Valley infrastructure, and later founded the AKASHA decentralized social project.
evidence_summary: Bitcoin Magazine (2011) and Ethereum co-founding (2013–14) are material and well documented, but eligibility requires a verified age ≤26 at the milestone; birth year was not found in reviewed sources.

name: Hugo Barra
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded mobile software startup Lobby7 in 1999 with MIT classmates and SoftBank investment at age ~22–23; the company was acquired by ScanSoft (later Nuance) in 2003.
early_history_summary: Born 28 October 1976 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. Studied at Colégio Pitágoras and briefly at UFMG before transferring to MIT in 1996, earning BS degrees in EECS and management science plus an M.Eng. in EECS; was MIT class of 2000 president and student commencement speaker. Co-founded Lobby7 while still at MIT.
family_context_summary: Born in Belo Horizonte, Brazil; early family financial/occupational detail not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT, SoftBank-backed startup, mobile speech tech, Brazilian-to-US pipeline
evidence_summary: MIT credentials, class leadership, and SoftBank-backed Lobby7 at ~23 established early operator credibility. Acquisition into ScanSoft/Nuance put him on speech/mobile product tracks that later fed Google Android, Xiaomi global expansion, Meta/Oculus VR, Detect, and Dreamer//dev/agents. Family background remains thinly documented; MIT network and mobile platform waves were the main accelerants.
starting_point: Born 28 October 1976 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil; educated at Colégio Pitágoras and UFMG before transferring to MIT.
current_position: Joined Meta Superintelligence Labs in 2026 with the Dreamer//dev/agents team after co-founding the AI agents startup; previously Detect CEO, Meta VR/Oculus VP, Xiaomi global VP, and Google Android VP.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Lobby7 with MIT classmates and SoftBank investment.
MIT Class of 2000 president and student commencement speaker; completed BS/M.Eng.
Lobby7 acquired by ScanSoft (later Nuance); led speech-to-text product work.
Joined Google; later became VP of Android product management and public spokesperson.
Left Google for Xiaomi as VP of Global Operations, leading international expansion.
Joined Facebook as VP of VR and head of Oculus.
Co-founded /dev/agents (later Dreamer), an AI personal agents startup.
Dreamer team joined Meta Superintelligence Labs.
